subsystems.name: Electrode threads
subsystems.role: Fine flexible wires that pick up electrical spikes from individual neurons.

subsystems.name: Implant electronics
subsystems.role: Amplifies, digitizes and wirelessly transmits neural signals.

subsystems.name: Surgical robot
subsystems.role: Inserts threads without damaging blood vessels.

subsystems.name: Wireless link
subsystems.role: Sends data out and power in through the intact scalp.

subsystems.name: Decoding software
subsystems.role: Translates neural activity into commands for computers or prosthetics.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate threads
buildSteps.detail: Photolithography patterns gold or platinum electrodes and traces onto a thin biocompatible polymer film, which is cut into many flexible threads.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the implant
buildSteps.detail: Threads are bonded to a custom chip that amplifies and digitizes signals; the electronics are sealed in a hermetic, body-safe package.

buildSteps.title: Build and calibrate the robot
buildSteps.detail: A surgical robot with micron-scale positioning and optical imaging is programmed to map and avoid surface blood vessels.

buildSteps.title: Implant
buildSteps.detail: A small opening is made in the skull; the robot inserts each thread to a precise depth in the cortex, and the implant is seated flush with the skull.

buildSteps.title: Close and pair
buildSteps.detail: The incision is closed, and the implant is wirelessly paired with an external device for power and data.

buildSteps.title: Decode and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Algorithms learn the patient's neural patterns over weeks, mapping intended movements to cursor or robotic actions.

buildSteps.title: Maintain and update
buildSteps.detail: Software updates, battery checks and monitoring for biocompatibility continue for the life of the implant.

prerequisites.why: threads must move with the brain without causing scarring.
recording from many neurons individually requires electrodes smaller than a human hair.
electronics must survive years in salt water and immune attack.
wires through the skin risk infection.
turning spike trains into reliable commands is hard and varies per patient.
avoiding blood vessels and hitting the right area is essential.

pathway.milestone: early human trials focus on letting paralysed patients control a cursor or keyboard
pathway.unlocks: proof of safety and basic function.

pathway.milestone: expanded trials for speech decoding, motor restoration and other conditions
pathway.unlocks: broader medical use and larger patient numbers.

pathway.milestone: higher channel counts and two-way interfaces
regulatory approval as a medical device and possible non-medical applications
pathway.unlocks: routine clinical use, with ethical and privacy frameworks.
